definitions.explanation: A collection of people or things organized together.
A group of students studying together.
Used as a counter for sets or pairs of items.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}は３{年|ねん}２{組|くみ}です。
{二人|ふたり}{組|ぐみ}で{練習|れんしゅう}する。
examples.notes: [Note: 組 becomes ぐみ when used as a suffix]

examples.japanese: このグラス{一組|ひとくみ}ください。
examples.english: One set of these glasses, please.

notes:
{組|くみ} refers to organized groups or sets.

AS SCHOOL CLASS:
- ３{年|ねん}２{組|くみ} (Year 3, Class 2)
- {同|おな}じ{組|くみ} (same class)

AS SUFFIX (becomes ぐみ):
- {二人|ふたり}{組|ぐみ} (pair, duo)
- {三人|さんにん}{組|ぐみ} (trio)
- {親子|おやこ}{組|ぐみ} (parent-child pair)

AS SET:
- {一組|ひとくみ} (one set)
- {茶碗|ちゃわん}{一組|ひとくみ} (a set of tea bowls)

RELATED WORDS:
- {組|く}む (to form a group)
- {組合|くみあい} (union, association)
